chunks: What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṭāṭarī, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥanẓalah, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me: “The qāmah and the two qāmahs are the cubit and the two cubits in the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام.”

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the authority transmitting the ruling
key_terms.الذِّرَاعَانِ: two cubits; the unit by which the two qāmahs are clarified
key_terms.الذِّرَاعُ: the cubit; the unit by which the qāmah is clarified
key_terms.الْقَامَةُ: a measured unit used here for determining prayer time, explained as one cubit
key_terms.الْقَامَتَانِ: two measured units used here for determining prayer time, explained as two cubits
key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: the written compilation attributed to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, cited as the source of this ruling

ai.seo_question: What do الْقَامَةُ and الْقَامَتَانِ mean in the timing of ẓuhr and ʿaṣr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal measure related to the timing of salat, clarifying that the terms qāmah and two qāmahs correspond to one cubit and two cubits in the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام. It reflects the transmission of precise ritual rulings from the Imams عليهم السلام in matters of worship.
